newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Clarke denies he is isolated over EMU.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Clarke denies he is isolated over EMU.

text.p: British Health Secretary Stephen Dorrell had no intention of changing the government's wait-and-see stance on European Monetary Union with remarks he made at the weekend, Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke told BBC radio on Monday.
Dorrell said in a television interview on Sunday that Britain would not be amongst the first wave of currencies joining EMU but then retracted his comments in a statement.

"Stephen declared yesterday in a statement which he gave that he had not intended to change the policy that he adhered to, the policy which is, in my opinion the only sensible policy," Clarke, the leading Europhile in the Conservative government, said.
Clarke said there was a collective policy on EMU and he denied that he was at odds with his cabinet colleagues. "This is not a policy on which I'm isolated in the cabinet."
He added that it was vital for British interests to remain properly involved in decisions on the future of Europe.
